meaning:
κυκλόω, -ῶ
(κύκλος), [in LXX chiefly for סָבַב ;]
1. to move in a circle, revolve.
2. to surround, encircle: with accusative of person(s), Jhn.10:24 (WH, txt., cf. -εύω), Act.14:20; pass., Luk.21:20, Heb.11:30 (cf. περι-κυκλόω).†
(AS)
glosses: after the people had marched around them

renderings.bsb: after the people had marched around them

elsewhere.note: “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is at hand.
The Jews therefore came around him and said to him, “How long will you hold us in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.”
But as the disciples stood around him, he rose up, and entered into the city. On the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.
By faith, the walls of Jericho fell down, after they had been encircled for seven days.
